rationale: The primary clinical series delineating DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder (Calame et al., 2023) evaluated axial hypotonia and documented it in 7 out of 14 individuals (50%). While hypotonia is a recurrent phenotypic feature reported across DHX9 cases (including Yamada et al., 2023 and OMIM #620988), empirical cohort data explicitly contradict the hypothesized frequency range of 70-85%.

evidence.text: In the primary cohort describing heterozygous pathogenic DHX9 variants in 20 individuals, axial hypotonia was evaluated and observed in 7 of 14 individuals (50%), directly refuting a 70-85% prevalence.

evidence.text: Yamada et al. identified hypotonia alongside severe developmental delay and feeding difficulties in patients with heterozygous DHX9 variants, supporting hypotonia as a characteristic clinical feature but without demonstrating a 70-85% cohort-wide frequency.

conflicts: The hypothesis posits that infantile and persistent axial hypotonia is present in roughly 70-85% of affected individuals across primary published series, whereas the largest systematic phenotypic assessment (Calame et al., 2023) documented axial hypotonia in only 50% (7/14) of evaluated individuals.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true frequency and natural history of axial versus peripheral hypotonia in DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder stratified by variant class (nuclear localization signal missense versus loss-of-function)?
new_directions.rationale: Calame et al. noted clear genotype-phenotype distinctions between LoF variants (milder NDD) and NLS missense variants (severe NDD); quantifying hypotonia separately across these classes could determine if specific subgroups achieve >70% frequency.

new_directions.question_text: Which combination of non-neurologic and dysmorphic features distinguishes DHX9-related disorder from closely related DExD/H-box helicase disorders (such as DHX30 and DDX6)?
new_directions.rationale: Hypotonia and intellectual disability are non-specific and shared across helicase-associated disorders; defining distinguishing phenotypic criteria is critical for clinical suspicion prior to molecular sequencing.
